text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
All papers lead with the death of Malacca state Chief Minister Mohd Zin Abdul Ghani without regaining consciousness following a stroke on Sunday.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysians must discard the attitude that local products were inferior to imported ones.

-- The Department of Civil Aviation is investigating "near misses" involving two Singapore Airlines airbus and a Malaysian Airlines aircraft over Perak state last Friday night, DCA director-general Zaini Omar said.
-- Carmaker Proton said it would only be affected by the yen's strength if the situation persists for longer than six or seven months, said DRB-Hicom group chairman Saleh Sulong.

-- Car distributor EON is looking at the legal and commercial aspects of a government proposal to restrict Proton car buyers from reselling their vehicles within a year, said DRB-Hicom group chairman Saleh Sulong.
-- Telekom Malaysia is keen to take up about 20 percent of Thailand's Samart which will cost about $200 million, industry sources said.
-- Forty-one golf clubs have been fined a total of 1.4 million ringgit for contravening Registrar of Companies' regulations, said registrar Ramly Ali.
